Use the OpenFOAM solver buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam.
Simulate natural convection in a 2D square cavity filled with air.
Use the Boussinesq approximation with reference temperature Tref = 295 K.
Set gravity to g = (0, -9.81, 0) m/s2.
Set the cavity side length to L = 0.0457 m so that the Rayleigh number is 10^5 when air properties are evaluated at 295 K.
Set the air transport properties to nu = 1.5e-5 m2/s, beta = 3.39e-3 1/K, and Pr = 0.71.
Set the left wall temperature boundary condition to fixedValue T = 300 K.
Set the right wall temperature boundary condition to fixedValue T = 290 K.
Set the top and bottom wall temperature boundary conditions to zeroGradient.
Set the velocity boundary condition on all four walls to noSlip.
Use a uniform Cartesian mesh with 128 by 128 cells.
Initialize the internal field temperature to 295 K, velocity to zero, and pressure to zero.
Run the simulation in laminar mode until steady state convergence is achieved.
